Title: March of the War Ghouls: NAC Storyline (May 31, 2012)

Messages.Author: echiang
Messages.Body:
The NAC Storyline during this past Origins was a resounding success! It was far beyond what I had anticipated or even hoped for.

Here is an initial report of some of the basic results. More details (including detailed game reports and deck lists) will follow.

Special thanks to all of the participants for helping to make this event so successful. And also thanks to Kevin Mergen and David Tatu for providing some prize support.

We had a total of 20 participants, which is only 3 shy of the 23 players that the Late Night Last Chance Qualifier that was run at the same time.

After several grueling and bloody rounds, Matt Morgan emerged victorious with the Brujah Antitribu.

His key minion choice was Hektor, who he brought out every turn. Backup choice is Miguel Santo Domingo for the extra bleed provided and for taking the Crusader Sword.

The field was very diverse, with 17 different clans represented by the 20 players (the duplicate clans were Brujah, Ravnos, and Ventrue):

- Since the Last Chance Qualifier ran long (didn't end until shortly before 7 P.M.), we opted to just go with 2 rounds and a final (instead of 3R + final).

- Many of the participants weren't aware of the storyline rules (having not seen the VEKN announcements or posts). To allow players to adapt their already existing decks to meet the crypt construction rules, I did allow the proxying of crypt (but not library) cards. I did not see anyone take advantage of this in my games, however.

- Bob Joseph had to leave after the first round, but this worked out well since Connor Bell missed the first round (he was in the Last Chance Qualifier Finals) and took over the seating spot, allowing us to maintain the same Optimal Seating chart.

Messages.Author: echiang
Messages.Body:
Placeholder for Game Reports

More details to follow.

My Round 1:

Table 1: Jeff Lake (Ravnos) -> Jen Goldberg (Osebo) -> Kevin Butcher (Salubri) -> David Litwin (True Brujah) -> Eric Chiang (Tremere Antitribu)

Notable Events:

- Goratrix and Saulot were both in play. They must have had some sort of kharmic connection because shortly after Goratrix got a Rutor's Hand, Saulot got one too.

- After I discarded an Autonomic Mastery, my prey (Ravnos) rushed me with a War Ghoul, which I promptly burned with my other copy of Autonomic Mastery. That was essentially a 4 pool swing, which put him in ousting range.

- The Salubri were bleeding the Trujah heavily (Repulsed Saulot and Repulsed Eurayle with a Pulse). Saulot had enough Anesthetic Touches to be safe from the War Ghouls, but I got him trapped in a hunting loop by rushing him with a War Ghoul and tapping Alejandro Aguirre to remove his only blood.

Meanwhile:

Table 3: Matt (!Brujah) ran into the Chaundice wall as his prey. After Chaundice tooled up with 2 Razor Bats and a Preternatural Strength, there was not much the !Brujah could do, so they got ousted by Ankur (!Salubri). The Gargoyles were down to 1 pool when time was called.

Table 4: I heard that there was some frustration with the Imbued, since War Ghouls can only rush vampires. In hindsight, I probably should have changed the DeMenTed War Ghouls to allow any minion rush. I really didn't expect to see Imbued though (Hugh chose it because it was his only deck that met the "clan" requirement).

My Round 2:

Table 3: Jared Strait (Blood Brothers) -> Eric Chiang (Tremere Antitribu) -> Brian Moritz (Gargoyles) -> Kelly Schultz (Ventrue) -> Connor Bell (Ventrue)

- The Tremere Antitribu as the predator to a Gargoyle deck (featuring Chaundice and Fustuk).

- Connor got off to a rough start. He brought out Mary Anne Blaire but after using her special, Freak Driving, and playing a superior Govern, his prey (Jared, Chicago Blood Brothers) thought that was too greedy. The Blood Brothers blocked with Gestalt. Torn Signpost + 2 additionals with Octopod removed Mary of all 9 of her blood, and she was finished with a Disarm and a diablerie action.

- Kelly (the other Ventrue) quickly became the table threat. This led to the "War Ghoul Alliance," whereby all of the remaining players agreed to spend one pool a turn to use a War Ghoul to rush the Ventrue. It started out with all 4 other players but we started the alliance a turn too late and Connor died soon after. Even against 3 War Ghoul rushes a turn, the Ventrue managed to survive through an obscene number of Majesties and a minion advantage (rescue/hunt). In the end, the Ventrue managed a table sweep despite us throwing about 20+ pool worth of War Ghouls at him.

Meanwhile:

Table 1: Lots of War Ghouls flying around, which hit Jeff Lake (Ravnos) really hard once he got out a Week of Nightmares. Not sure how that worked when his predator (Cory Seigel) was also playing Ravnos, though of the Anarch variety.

Table 2: I heard that Table 2 was fun with everyone playing equally bad decks. The Baali had 3 Anarch Revolts in play and his predator (Bill playing Brujah) was the only deck unable to get an anarch since Bill's predator (Jen playing Osebo) kept blocking his attempts. Needless to say, Jen got her 1 VP. Meanwhile, the !Salubri and the !Toreador (Miller/Greta combat) massacred each other, leaving an easy path to the game win for the Baali.

Table 4: Had the interesting dynamic of Brujah preying on True Brujah preying on Brujah Antitribu. In early Tension in the Ranks caused problems for the Brujah (Arms Dealer) deck. David Litwin's game description below covers more details.

FINALS:

I have fairly detailed notes which I will type up and post shortly. They cover most of what transpired in the middle and end of the game, but I wasn't quite as detailed early on (the challenges of playing & running the event at the same time).

Eric Chiang (Tremere Antitribu) -> Kelly Schultz (Ventrue) -> Matt Morgan (Brujah Antitribu) -> Jesper Boje (Baali) -> Hugh Angseesing (Imbued)

- Hugh wanted to get to a Battlestar game that was starting shortly, so he played without abandon going full forward. Unfortunately for him, Imbued don't do too well against Goratrix + Trap or Goratrix + Carrion Crows, so his ended up being a short game. He did spend 4 pool to burn Selena's Rack via a War Ghoul though.

- Jack "Hannibal137" Harmon had a Crusader Sword, IR Goggles, and Leather Jacket (along with Rejuvenate and Vigilance) when he blocked Goratrix's attempt to adopt a puppy (Underbridge Stray) and was incapacitated by Carrion Crows + innate steal, with Rego Motus to prevent the Crusader Sword.

- Afterwards, the Unnamed was determined to pillowface the Imbued. On his first try he was blocked by an untapped Imbued and so he Earth Melded. On his second try, he was blocked with an On the Qui Vive and he Earth Melded. On his third try, he was blocked with Angel of Berlin and he Earth Melded. On his fourth try, he was finally successful and so the Baali Methuselah gained possession of the Crusader Sword.

- Later on, the Unnamed was torporized by Hektor and the Brujah Antitribu (who have a thing for melee weapons) diablerized him, with Miguel Santo Domingo ending up with the sword. It was also interesting that the first two !Brujah that Matt Morgan brought up were Hektor and Sela, both of whom have had prior experiences with the Baali (Hektor associated with Maureen, Dark Priestess back in the Dark Ages and Sela had the whole Nergal affair). Looks like the !Brujah finally got their revenge on the Baali!

- There was some consternation among the Brujah Antitribu when the traitorous Armin Brenner showed up being influenced by the Ventrue. Of course they later reminded their clanmate of his sect loyalties when they visited a little street justice on him.

- When it was down to 3 players, both the Ventrue and the Tremere Antitribu were trying to help out the Brujah Antitribu.

Messages.Author: Pagan
Messages.Body:
I didn't have much chance to work on deck ideas as I was still moving in and waiting for my household goods so I only modified a deck to take.

I wanted to get the True Brujah some representation and figured no one else would play them, but the crypt rules made it rather hard to make a decent deck. I wasn't sure how much folks would even try to use the War Ghouls. This deck wasn't much good in local play but I figured storyline decks would be slower and give me time to actually do something.

I added the the extra Al-Muntaquims to make the crypt legal and removed the Setite support for bounce weenies. Other than that the deck intended to get guns cheap and/or free and surprise a War Ghoul rush with an Autonomic Mastery.

I didn't really take any notes of the storyline event as it was really just a fun tournament.

At the start of round 1 I remember telling people my deck will be much like the Trujah of V:TM. They'll show up, influence a few things, rant and rave about past transgressions, and ultimately have little impact on the overall events.

Al-Muntathir shows up early and a couple dom support minions, only to see Goratrix as my prey and Saulot as my predator. Sadly they couldn't start the game next to each other.

Saulot quickly gets a friend Euralye and Goratrix found the Ruins of Ceoris. Al was looking for some non-unique equipment to go get but I wasn't finding any in my hand and no one else had discarded anything.

Saulot and Euralye became unblockable by me with Repulsions on them so now I'm just trying to gain pool and hoping some War Ghoul rushes can take down Saulot. A few attempts were made and failed to do any damage.

My game still wasn't too bad as the !Tremere had failed to gain much pool so my small bleeds were keeping them in range. The Ravnos and Osebo were hurting each other too much to be any help to me.

After that point I don't remember what happened but the table fell apart rather quickly to a steamrolling Goratrix.

Round 2 ended up being more interesting and storyline related as the War Ghouls showed up a bit more and combat was much more prevalent.

My predator brings up Brujah weenies who got guns and used DBRs to make it agg, while my prey was using Hektor and his fearsome agg stealth and a few others.

My first turn Anarch Convert for the edge failed as he got rushed by my predator's War Ghoul. Al comes out on turn 3 and spends 2 turns getting rushed before he can Kiss of Lachesis away one of the Brujah's guns and then take it next turn. That gets me a gun with 1 blood left and forced to play wary in combat as my support team of Keith Moody and another dom minion won't be enough to have a significant impact.

Brujah beat on Trujah who beat on !Brujah who beat on Brujah with the quick exit of my crossable ally who I can;t even remember what clan he was.

The Trujah team up with the Brujah with a deal to rush the !Brujah. A bit of table wrangling back and forth as the Brujah were in no position to get a win as the Trujah could destroy any of their guns and the !Brujah combat was strong enough to win most fights they had.

I was looking at a chance for an oust and such but don't believe I ever got it as the !Brujah likely got the game win in round 2.

>
> Saulot and Euralye became unblockable by me with Repulsions on them so now I'm just trying to gain pool and hoping some War Ghoul rushes can take down Saulot. A few attempts were made and failed to do any damage.
>
> My game still wasn't too bad as the !Tremere had failed to gain much pool so my small bleeds were keeping them in range. The Ravnos and Osebo were hurting each other too much to be any help to me.
>
> After that point I don't remember what happened but the table fell apart rather quickly to a steamrolling Goratrix.
>
I never blocked Al-Muntathir because taking a bleed for 1 was preferable than the potential Domain of Evernight + Outside the Hourglass combo.

The Ravnos deck was a swarm deck and the Osebo were having a hard time dealing with all the minions. The Osebo had plenty of maneuvers to stay away from the War Ghouls though as did the Salubri have with Anesthetic Touch.

Turning point was when the Ravnos used a War Ghoul on me which I burned with Autonomic Mastery. That put him within ousting range and the Osebo were ousted soon after.

Key turning point for you was when Saulot played Unburdening the Bestial Soul on Al-Muntathir. You still managed to Heidelberg everything on to Robin, but your game was really shot at that point.

> Brujah beat on Trujah who beat on !Brujah who beat on Brujah with the quick exit of my crossable ally who I can;t even remember what clan he was.
>
Nosferatu Antitribu.

Then I decided to work a few Autonomic Mastery in to discourage War Ghouls rushing my support minions into the ground and as a nice surprise so I swapped it over to dominate.
>
For your 3 "non-clan or non-grouping" slots, did you consider:

Ian Forestal, Synesios, and/or Krassimir?

Of course it would have made your crypt size bigger (with no weenie support) but maybe a Villein strategy could have afforded it? Maybe not Synesios/Krassimir with the scarce cost, but Ian Forestal seems like he could have fit in nicely.

Responding to Kraus, I imagine weenie AUS would have worked nicely: Isabel de Leon, Martin Franckel, Veejay Vinod, Zoe, though they would have been vulnerable to the War Ghouls in a way the dominate weenies (with Autonomic Mastery) were not.
